question: Can a class-balanced, calibrated gradient-boosting model give more accurate and better-calibrated music-emotion suggestions than a standard random forest on a public music-audio feature dataset?
method: Stratified 80/20 split (seed 42); preprocessing fitted on train only; baseline random forest with default settings vs class-balanced LightGBM with isotonic calibration (hyper-parameters chosen by 5-fold CV on train). Both run with seeds 42, 43, 44; test set used once per model.
baseline: Standard RandomForestClassifier with default settings (generic suggestion model).
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM classifier (class_weight='balanced', small CV grid on train) with cross-validated isotonic probability calibration.
notes: Single stratified split, so the test set is small (about 80 songs) and differences are noisy; the three seeds capture model randomness only, not split variability. Isotonic calibration is fitted by internal CV on a small training set and can be noisy. Brier score is a calibration proxy for trust, not a user-trust measurement. This is a stand-in experiment; the motivating paper's model and results are not stated and are not reproduced. The ucimlrepo import of dataset 862 is refused by the service ('not available for import'), so the script falls back to downloading the same official UCI zip directly; the data content is identical.
